### Plans

#### Public Plans

* [`ovadm::add_agent`](#ovadm--add_agent): Add one or more agent nodes to an existing OpenVox Server deployment
* [`ovadm::add_compiler`](#ovadm--add_compiler): Add one or more compiler nodes to an existing OpenVox Server deployment
* [`ovadm::backup`](#ovadm--backup): Back up an OpenVox primary server to one archive
* [`ovadm::install`](#ovadm--install): Install a new OpenVox Server deployment
* [`ovadm::restore`](#ovadm--restore): Restore an OpenVox primary server from an `ovadm::backup` archive
* [`ovadm::status`](#ovadm--status): Check the status of an OpenVox Server deployment
* [`ovadm::upgrade`](#ovadm--upgrade): Upgrade an existing OpenVox Server deployment

#### Private Plans

* `ovadm::subplans::agent_enroll`: Enroll agent hosts with the CA and apply their first catalog
* `ovadm::subplans::agent_install`: Install OpenVox Server on compiler hosts, with the server as their CA
* `ovadm::subplans::agent_package`: Install openvox-agent on agent hosts and point them at the server
* `ovadm::subplans::cert_setup`: Submit and sign certificates for compiler hosts
* `ovadm::subplans::configure`: Configure puppet.conf on an OpenVox Server node
* `ovadm::subplans::install`: Install OpenVox Server packages on a target
* `ovadm::subplans::precheck`: Validate that a target is ready to run OpenVox Server
* `ovadm::subplans::restore_pass`: One pass of a restore: the files of a scope, then the server up
* `ovadm::subplans::upgrade_compilers`: Upgrade openvox-server on compiler pool nodes
* `ovadm::subplans::upgrade_repo`: Move nodes to the package repository of the major version they are upgraded to
* `ovadm::subplans::upgrade_server`: Upgrade openvox-server on a single node

## Functions

### <a name="ovadm--version"></a>`ovadm::version`

Type: Puppet Language

Read rather than hardcoded: the release workflow refuses a tag that
disagrees with metadata.json, so the file is the source of truth.

#### `ovadm::version()`

Read rather than hardcoded: the release workflow refuses a tag that
disagrees with metadata.json, so the file is the source of truth.

Returns: `String` the version, or `unknown` when metadata.json has none

## Data types

### <a name="Ovadm--Backup_opts"></a>`Ovadm::Backup_opts`

Every item is on unless switched off, so the default is everything a
disaster recovery needs and a caller opts out of what it does not want.

- `ca`: the CA directory, the server's own certificate and key, and
  OpenVoxDB's copy of them
- `config`: the rest of `/etc/puppetlabs/` (without `code/`) and the
  services' environment files
- `code`: what r10k deployed, as each environment's `.r10k-deploy.json`
  and `hiera.yaml`, with `/etc/puppetlabs/r10k/`; `include_code_tree` on
  the plan takes the directory too

Alias of

```puppet
Struct[{
  Optional[ca]     => Boolean,
  Optional[config] => Boolean,
  Optional[code]   => Boolean,
}]
```

## Tasks

### <a name="agent_runonce"></a>`agent_runonce`

Run the Puppet agent once and return the exit status

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `waitforcert`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Seconds to wait for a certificate to be signed (0 = submit CSR and exit immediately)

##### `environment`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Environment to run against, passed as --environment. Omitted, the agent uses the environment the server assigned on its last run, falling back to puppet.conf; with it, the agent asks for this one and the run fails if the server does not have it

### <a name="backup_create"></a>`backup_create`

Back up an OpenVox primary server into one archive under destination: the selected items' files as they are on the host, a manifest of the host (versions, gems, deployed code, CA serial, OpenVoxDB schema) and the topology the server sees, with checksums of every file. Returns the archive path and size

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `destination`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Directory for the archive, created 0700 if missing. Default /var/backups/openvox

##### `ca`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Include the CA directory, the server's own certificate and key, and OpenVoxDB's copy of them. Default true

##### `config`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Include the rest of /etc/puppetlabs (without code/) and the services' environment files. Default true

##### `code`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Include each environment's .r10k-deploy.json and hiera.yaml, the record of what r10k deployed, and /etc/puppetlabs/r10k. Default true

##### `include_code_tree`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

With code, take /etc/puppetlabs/code itself. Default false

##### `extra_paths`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Comma-separated absolute paths outside /etc/puppetlabs to include, such as the r10k deploy key. Each must exist

##### `stop_services`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Stop puppetserver and puppetdb while the files are copied, and start them again afterwards. Default false

##### `age_recipient`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

An age public key; the archive is encrypted to it and named .tar.gz.age. age must be installed

##### `ovadm_version`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Recorded in the manifest; the plan passes its own version

### <a name="backup_restore"></a>`backup_restore`

Put the files of an ovadm::backup_create archive back on the host it came from: checks every checksum, the certname, the openvox-server version and that the host's CA has signed nothing the archive does not know, stops the running services, extracts the items in scope with owners and modes as archived, skipping *.rpmnew and the like, and starts the services again. Reports which files changed, which were missing, and which gems from the manifest are not installed

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `archive`

Data type: `String[1]`

Path of the archive on this host

##### `scope`

Data type: `Optional[Pattern[/\A(ca|config|code|extra)(,(ca|config|code|extra))*\z/]]`

Comma-separated items to put back: ca, config, code (with /etc/puppetlabs/r10k), extra. Default: everything the archive holds

##### `exclude`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Comma-separated absolute paths within the scope to leave out of this pass

##### `force`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Restore even when the certname or the openvox-server version differ, or the host's CA has signed certificates since the backup. Default false

##### `dry_run`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Report what would change and touch nothing. Default false

##### `age_identity`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Path of an age identity file, needed to read a .tar.gz.age archive

### <a name="backup_verify"></a>`backup_verify`

Check an archive that ovadm::backup_create wrote: it unpacks, every file matches its checksum, the manifest is present, and (with check_host) it is from this host and its package versions match. Problems are reported in the result as status failed; package differences as warnings

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `archive`

Data type: `String[1]`

Path of the archive on this host

##### `check_host`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Compare the manifest's certname and package versions with this host. Default true

##### `age_identity`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Path of an age identity file, needed to read a .tar.gz.age archive

### <a name="ca_setup"></a>`ca_setup`

Create the CA with `puppetserver ca setup` (root + intermediate, 15-year lifetime) before the first service start. Skipped when a CA already exists.

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `subject_alt_names`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Comma-separated DNS alt names to embed in the server certificate (--subject-alt-names)

##### `certname`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Certificate name for the server certificate (--certname); defaults to the certname in puppet.conf

##### `ca_name`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Common name for the intermediate CA certificate (--ca-name); defaults to 'Puppet CA: <fqdn>'

### <a name="configure_ca_renewal"></a>`configure_ca_renewal`

Set certificate auto-renewal settings in ca.conf on the CA. Takes effect on the next puppetserver (re)start and only affects certificates signed after that.

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `allow_auto_renewal`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether the CA honors agent certificate renewal requests (certificate-authority.allow-auto-renewal)

##### `auto_renewal_cert_ttl`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

TTL for auto-renewed certificates, e.g. '60d' (certificate-authority.auto-renewal-cert-ttl); omit to keep the packaged value

### <a name="configure_compiler_ssl"></a>`configure_compiler_ssl`

Configure puppetserver SSL on a compiler to use the puppet-CA-signed node certificate

**Supports noop?** false

### <a name="configure_puppet_conf"></a>`configure_puppet_conf`

Write /etc/puppetlabs/puppet/puppet.conf with server identity and optional DNS alt names, keeping the directory settings (vardir, ssldir, ...) an existing [main] section sets

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `certname`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Certificate name for this node; defaults to the system FQDN

##### `server`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Hostname of the OpenVox Server; defaults to the system FQDN

##### `ca_server`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

CA server hostname; set on compilers to point to the server

##### `dns_alt_names`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Comma-separated list of DNS alternative names for the server certificate

##### `environment`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Puppet environment for this node's agent ([agent] environment); omit for the server's default

### <a name="configure_repo"></a>`configure_repo`

Configure the OpenVox package repository for this OS, removing the release packages of other OpenVox and Puppet major versions. With apt_base_url or yum_base_url, the release package comes from that mirror and its repository file is pointed at it

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `ovox_major`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

OpenVox major version (e.g. 8)

##### `apt_base_url`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Base URL of a mirror of apt.voxpupuli.org, with the same layout: the release package is downloaded from it, and the repository file points at it. Defaults to https://apt.voxpupuli.org

##### `yum_base_url`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Base URL of a mirror of yum.voxpupuli.org, with the same layout: the release package is downloaded from it, and the repository file points at it. Defaults to https://yum.voxpupuli.org

### <a name="os_identification"></a>`os_identification`

Detect OS family, name, version, and architecture

**Supports noop?** false

### <a name="precheck"></a>`precheck`

Validate target readiness: OS family, Java version, port 8140, host firewall, NTP sync, and enough memory for OpenVox Server's heap; for an agent host, OS family and NTP sync only

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `role`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['server', 'agent']]`

What the host is about to become: 'server' (the default; also a compiler) checks everything, 'agent' checks the OS family and time sync only, since an agent needs no Java, heap memory or 8140

##### `upgrade`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Check a host ovadm::upgrade is about to upgrade. A Java below the supported versions is a warning rather than a failure, since the upgrade installs and selects one.

##### `ovox_major`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[8]]`

The OpenVox major version about to be installed or upgraded to, when known. On 9 and later the server picks its own Java through a launcher, so the system java is not checked. A host where the launcher is already installed is checked against the Java it runs, whatever this says.

### <a name="select_java"></a>`select_java`

Make sure the installed openvox-server has a supported Java: on 8, point the java alternative at Java 17 or 21 when the default is neither; on packages with a Java launcher (9), leave the alternative alone and check that the launcher finds one

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `pp_role`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]*\z/]`

Value to embed as the pp_role certificate extension (e.g. openvox_compiler): letters, digits and _ . : -, starting with a letter or digit

### <a name="sign_csr"></a>`sign_csr`

### <a name="topology"></a>`topology`

Report the deployment topology from the primary server: certname and whether it is the CA, the compilers (signed certificates carrying pp_role=openvox_compiler), where puppetdb.conf sends OpenVoxDB traffic, the OpenVoxDB package and database connection on this host, and the local PostgreSQL. Reads files and packages only, so it works with the services stopped

**Supports noop?** false

### <a name="wait_until_service_ready"></a>`wait_until_service_ready`

Poll until puppetserver responds on port 8140 or a timeout expires. On a timeout, the error says why: the service state and the last error puppetserver logged, such as its startup memory check

**Supports noop?** false

#### Parameters

##### `max_wait`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Maximum seconds to wait before failing (default: 300)

## Plans

### <a name="ovadm--add_agent"></a>`ovadm::add_agent`

Installs `openvox-agent` on stock hosts from the workstation, points them at
the server (or a compiler or load balancer), signs their certificates on the
server and runs each agent once, so every host applies its first catalog
inside the plan. The agent service is left as the package leaves it: ovadm
does not schedule runs.

A host that fails a step is left out of the following ones and reported at
the end, with the hosts that got through; the plan then fails, so a batch
with one bad host still enrolls the others.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `ovadm::add_agent` plan:

* [`server_host`](#-ovadm--add_agent--server_host)
* [`agent_hosts`](#-ovadm--add_agent--agent_hosts)
* [`agent_server`](#-ovadm--add_agent--agent_server)
* [`ovox_version`](#-ovadm--add_agent--ovox_version)
* [`apt_base_url`](#-ovadm--add_agent--apt_base_url)
* [`yum_base_url`](#-ovadm--add_agent--yum_base_url)
* [`environment`](#-ovadm--add_agent--environment)
* [`pp_role`](#-ovadm--add_agent--pp_role)

##### <a name="-ovadm--add_agent--server_host"></a>`server_host`

Data type: `TargetSpec`

The OpenVox Server (acts as CA)

##### <a name="-ovadm--add_agent--agent_hosts"></a>`agent_hosts`

Data type: `TargetSpec`

The agent node(s) to install and enroll

##### <a name="-ovadm--add_agent--agent_server"></a>`agent_server`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

The name the agents ask for catalogs from, written as `server` in their
`puppet.conf`. Defaults to the server's FQDN; on a Large topology, give a
compiler's FQDN or the load balancer's name in front of the pool. The CA
is always the server

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-ovadm--add_agent--ovox_version"></a>`ovox_version`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

OpenVox Agent version to install (e.g. '8.30.0'); determines which major
repo to enable. Omitted, the agents get the newest agent of the major the
server runs

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-ovadm--add_agent--apt_base_url"></a>`apt_base_url`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Base URL of an apt mirror to use instead of https://apt.voxpupuli.org

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-ovadm--add_agent--yum_base_url"></a>`yum_base_url`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Base URL of a yum/dnf mirror to use instead of https://yum.voxpupuli.org

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-ovadm--add_agent--environment"></a>`environment`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Puppet environment the agents ask for from their first run on
(`environment` in the `[agent]` section of `puppet.conf`, and
`--environment` on the runs inside the plan); omit for the server's
default, `production`. It must exist on the server already: a run against
an environment the server does not have fails

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-ovadm--add_agent--pp_role"></a>`pp_role`

Data type: `Optional[Pattern[/\A[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]*\z/]]`

Role to put in the agents' certificates, as the `pp_role` extension
(`$trusted['extensions']['pp_role']`), for sites that classify on it. The
plan sets it in `csr_attributes.yaml` before the first agent run,
keeping whatever else a file already there holds (a `challengePassword`
for policy-based autosigning, other extensions); omitted, the file is
left alone. One role
for every host in the run. It takes effect when the certificate is
signed, so a host that already has one keeps the role it was signed with.
`openvox_server` and `openvox_compiler`, ovadm's roles for the server and
compilers, are refused

Default value: `undef`

### <a name="ovadm--backup"></a>`ovadm::backup`

Takes the CA, the server's certificates, its configuration and a record of
the deployed code from the server into one archive under `destination`,
with a manifest of the host it came from and the topology the server sees,
then checks the archive against its own checksums. Copying the archive off
the host is left to you: it holds the CA's private key.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `ovadm::backup` plan:

* [`server_host`](#-ovadm--backup--server_host)
* [`destination`](#-ovadm--backup--destination)
* [`backup`](#-ovadm--backup--backup)
* [`include_code_tree`](#-ovadm--backup--include_code_tree)
* [`extra_paths`](#-ovadm--backup--extra_paths)
* [`stop_services`](#-ovadm--backup--stop_services)
* [`age_recipient`](#-ovadm--backup--age_recipient)
* [`verify`](#-ovadm--backup--verify)

##### <a name="-ovadm--backup--server_host"></a>`server_host`

Data type: `TargetSpec`

The OpenVox Server node

##### <a name="-ovadm--backup--destination"></a>`destination`

Data type: `String[1]`

Directory on the server for the archive. Created with mode 0700 if it
does not exist.

Default value: `'/var/backups/openvox'`

##### <a name="-ovadm--backup--backup"></a>`backup`

Data type: `Ovadm::Backup_opts`

What to include; everything is on unless switched off. See
`Ovadm::Backup_opts`.

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-ovadm--backup--include_code_tree"></a>`include_code_tree`

Data type: `Boolean`

Take `/etc/puppetlabs/code/` itself, not only the record of what r10k
deployed. For sites whose git server shares the primary's blast radius.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-ovadm--backup--extra_paths"></a>`extra_paths`

Data type: `Array[String[1]]`

Paths outside `/etc/puppetlabs/` to include, such as the r10k deploy key
or the systemd units that run r10k. Each must exist.

Default value: `[]`

##### <a name="-ovadm--backup--stop_services"></a>`stop_services`

Data type: `Boolean`

Stop puppetserver and puppetdb while the files are copied, and start
them again afterwards. Off by default: the CA directory changes only
when a certificate is signed or revoked, and the plan reports if that
happened during the copy.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-ovadm--backup--age_recipient"></a>`age_recipient`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

An `age` public key. When set, the archive is encrypted to it and gets
the suffix `.age`; `age` must be installed on the server.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-ovadm--backup--verify"></a>`verify`

Data type: `Boolean`

Check the archive's checksums and manifest after writing it. Skipped
for an encrypted archive, which the server cannot read back: run
`ovadm::backup_verify` with `age_identity` where the identity is.

Default value: `true`

### <a name="ovadm--install"></a>`ovadm::install`

Runs prechecks, configures the package repository, installs openvox-server,
writes puppet.conf, and waits for the service to become ready.
When compiler_hosts is provided, installs a Large topology.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `ovadm::install` plan:

* [`server_host`](#-ovadm--install--server_host)
* [`compiler_hosts`](#-ovadm--install--compiler_hosts)
* [`ovox_version`](#-ovadm--install--ovox_version)
* [`ovox_server_version`](#-ovadm--install--ovox_server_version)
* [`dns_alt_names`](#-ovadm--install--dns_alt_names)
* [`enable_cert_auto_renewal`](#-ovadm--install--enable_cert_auto_renewal)
* [`auto_renewal_cert_ttl`](#-ovadm--install--auto_renewal_cert_ttl)
* [`apt_base_url`](#-ovadm--install--apt_base_url)
* [`yum_base_url`](#-ovadm--install--yum_base_url)
* [`package_url`](#-ovadm--install--package_url)
* [`environment`](#-ovadm--install--environment)

##### <a name="-ovadm--install--server_host"></a>`server_host`

Data type: `TargetSpec`

The OpenVox Server node

##### <a name="-ovadm--install--compiler_hosts"></a>`compiler_hosts`

Data type: `Optional[TargetSpec]`

One or more compiler nodes (Large topology)

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-ovadm--install--ovox_version"></a>`ovox_version`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

OpenVox Agent version (e.g. '8.26.2'); determines which major repo to enable

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-ovadm--install--ovox_server_version"></a>`ovox_server_version`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Specific openvox-server version to install (e.g. '8.13.0'); omit for latest

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-ovadm--install--dns_alt_names"></a>`dns_alt_names`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String[1]]]`

DNS alternative names to embed in the server certificate.
Useful when agents connect via a load balancer hostname or alias.
They are passed to `puppetserver ca setup`, which creates the server
certificate at install time. Adding alt names later means regenerating
that certificate.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-ovadm--install--enable_cert_auto_renewal"></a>`enable_cert_auto_renewal`

Data type: `Boolean`

Enable certificate auto-renewal on the CA (allow-auto-renewal in
ca.conf) before first service start, so every certificate the CA signs
is short-lived and renewed automatically during agent runs.
NOTE: renewal only happens when agents run regularly (service, cron,
or scheduled runs) — ovadm does not set that up. Nodes that stop
checking in are left with an expired certificate once the short TTL
elapses. Compilers additionally need a puppetserver restart to serve
a renewed certificate. Defaults to false, matching upstream.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-ovadm--install--auto_renewal_cert_ttl"></a>`auto_renewal_cert_ttl`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

TTL for auto-renewed certificates (e.g. '60d', '90d'). Only used when
enable_cert_auto_renewal is true; omit to keep the packaged default.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-ovadm--install--apt_base_url"></a>`apt_base_url`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Base URL of an apt mirror to use instead of https://apt.voxpupuli.org

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-ovadm--install--yum_base_url"></a>`yum_base_url`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Base URL of a yum/dnf mirror to use instead of https://yum.voxpupuli.org

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-ovadm--install--package_url"></a>`package_url`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Direct URL to an openvox-server rpm or deb to install instead of the
repository's package. The repository is still configured, for dependencies.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-ovadm--install--environment"></a>`environment`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Puppet environment the nodes' agents ask for from their first run on
(`environment` in the `[agent]` section of `puppet.conf`); omit for the
server's default, `production`. Matters where that first run applies the
site's code to the server or compiler: a control-repo whose pins for this
deployment live in another environment would otherwise be applied from
`production`, moving the packages ovadm just installed.

Default value: `undef`

### <a name="ovadm--restore"></a>`ovadm::restore`

Puts the files of the archive back on the host they came from, with the
services stopped for the copy, then starts puppetserver, redeploys the code
when it is in scope, runs the agent once so the site's own code converges,
and reports the status. The archive is checked first: its checksums, that
it is from this host, that the openvox-server version matches, and, when
the CA is in scope, that the CA on the host has signed nothing since the
backup. Each check stops the plan unless `force` is set.

Files added since the backup stay. On a host the openvox_server module
manages, the files it owns come back on the next agent run: roll those
back in Hiera, and use this plan for the rest.

On a rebuilt host, run `ovadm::install` first with the versions the
manifest names (the plan prints the exact command when the server is not
installed), then this plan with `rebuild`. That restores everything but
`puppet.conf`, `puppetdb.conf` and `routes.yaml` first and runs the agent
on a server that has no OpenVoxDB wiring yet, as on the original build,
so the site's code can bring OpenVoxDB back; then it puts the
configuration back whole, with `openvoxdb-termini` installed when the
host still lacks it.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `ovadm::restore` plan:

* [`server_host`](#-ovadm--restore--server_host)
* [`archive`](#-ovadm--restore--archive)
* [`source`](#-ovadm--restore--source)
* [`scope`](#-ovadm--restore--scope)
* [`rebuild`](#-ovadm--restore--rebuild)
* [`force`](#-ovadm--restore--force)
* [`dry_run`](#-ovadm--restore--dry_run)
* [`age_identity`](#-ovadm--restore--age_identity)
* [`deploy_code`](#-ovadm--restore--deploy_code)
* [`agent_run`](#-ovadm--restore--agent_run)

##### <a name="-ovadm--restore--server_host"></a>`server_host`

Data type: `TargetSpec`

The OpenVox Server node

##### <a name="-ovadm--restore--archive"></a>`archive`

Data type: `String[1]`

Path of the archive on the server

##### <a name="-ovadm--restore--source"></a>`source`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Path of the archive on the workstation running Bolt. It is uploaded to
`archive` on the server before anything else: the rebuilt-server path,
where the archive is wherever the backups were kept.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-ovadm--restore--scope"></a>`scope`

Data type: `Optional[Array[Enum['ca', 'config', 'code', 'extra'], 1]]`

What to put back: `ca`, `config`, `code` (what the archive holds under
`/etc/puppetlabs/code/` and `/etc/puppetlabs/r10k/`, followed by an r10k
deploy), `extra` (the paths given as `extra_paths` at backup time).
Default: everything the archive holds.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-ovadm--restore--rebuild"></a>`rebuild`

Data type: `Boolean`

The host was rebuilt: leave the files that wire the server to OpenVoxDB
out of the first pass, run the agent so the site's code brings back
what it installs, then put the configuration back whole.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-ovadm--restore--force"></a>`force`

Data type: `Boolean`

Restore even when the archive is from another certname or
openvox-server version, or the host's CA has signed certificates since
the backup; those certificates must then be cleaned and re-signed.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-ovadm--restore--dry_run"></a>`dry_run`

Data type: `Boolean`

Report which files would change and stop; nothing is written and no
service is touched.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-ovadm--restore--age_identity"></a>`age_identity`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Path of the age identity file on the server, for a `.tar.gz.age` archive.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-ovadm--restore--deploy_code"></a>`deploy_code`

Data type: `Boolean`

With `code` in scope, run `r10k deploy environment --modules` after the
files are back, when r10k is installed.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-ovadm--restore--agent_run"></a>`agent_run`

Data type: `Boolean`

Run the agent once on the server after the restore, so the site's code
brings back what it owns. A failed run is reported, not fatal: the files
are back and the services are up by then.

Default value: `true`

### <a name="ovadm--status"></a>`ovadm::status`

Check the status of an OpenVox Server deployment

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `ovadm::status` plan:

* [`server_host`](#-ovadm--status--server_host)

##### <a name="-ovadm--status--server_host"></a>`server_host`

Data type: `TargetSpec`

The target node running OpenVox Server

### <a name="ovadm--upgrade"></a>`ovadm::upgrade`

Upgrades within a major version, to a new major version (8 to 9), and from
Puppet Server to OpenVox (7 to 8). The server is upgraded first, then the
compilers.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `ovadm::upgrade` plan:

* [`server_host`](#-ovadm--upgrade--server_host)
* [`ovox_server_version`](#-ovadm--upgrade--ovox_server_version)
* [`compiler_hosts`](#-ovadm--upgrade--compiler_hosts)
* [`package_url`](#-ovadm--upgrade--package_url)
* [`ovox_major`](#-ovadm--upgrade--ovox_major)
* [`apt_base_url`](#-ovadm--upgrade--apt_base_url)
* [`yum_base_url`](#-ovadm--upgrade--yum_base_url)

##### <a name="-ovadm--upgrade--server_host"></a>`server_host`

Data type: `TargetSpec`

The OpenVox Server node

##### <a name="-ovadm--upgrade--ovox_server_version"></a>`ovox_server_version`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

The openvox-server version to upgrade to (e.g. '8.13.0'). Its major version
is the one the nodes move to.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-ovadm--upgrade--compiler_hosts"></a>`compiler_hosts`

Data type: `Optional[TargetSpec]`

Compiler pool nodes to upgrade (Large topology)

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-ovadm--upgrade--package_url"></a>`package_url`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Direct URL to an openvox-server rpm or deb to install instead of the
repository's package

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-ovadm--upgrade--ovox_major"></a>`ovox_major`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[8]]`

The OpenVox major version to upgrade to. Defaults to the major version of
ovox_server_version; set it when upgrading to a new major from package_url
alone.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-ovadm--upgrade--apt_base_url"></a>`apt_base_url`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Base URL of an apt mirror to use instead of https://apt.voxpupuli.org, for
nodes that move to a new major version's repository

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-ovadm--upgrade--yum_base_url"></a>`yum_base_url`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Base URL of a yum/dnf mirror to use instead of https://yum.voxpupuli.org,
for nodes that move to a new major version's repository

Default value: `undef`
